description: The image is a single rendered data table (Table 2), not a plot or micrograph. Its column headers read, left to right: an unlabelled alloy-name column, "YS, MPa", "TS, MPa", "TEL, %", "TS × TEL, GPa-%" and "Reference". Thirty-five rows list room-temperature tensile results. The reference entries cover Fe–Al binary alloys Fe-8Al to Fe-12Al [42]; Fe-10Mn [43], Fe-24Mn and Fe-30Mn [44]; Fe-14Mn-1.05C and Fe-14Mn-3Al-1.05C [45]; Fe-18Mn-0.6C and Fe-18Mn-3Al-0.6C [46]; Fe-22Mn-0.5C [47]; Fe-21Mn-6Al-1C-3Si [14]; five rows of Fe-28Mn-12Al-1C (TRIPLEX steel) [36]; Fe-30Mn-8Al-1.2C (TRIPLEX steel) [48]; two rows each for Fe-17Cr-6.5Ni-1.2Mn (301LN stainless steel) [49] and Fe-18Cr-9Ni-1.8Mn (304 stainless steel) [50]. The last four rows are the paper's own steels, marked "This study": Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-3Cr (969/1141 MPa, 54.4%, 62.07 GPa-%), Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni (1202/1283 MPa, 34.1%, 43.75 GPa-%), Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni3Cr (1110/1206 MPa, 45.9%, 55.36 GPa-%) and Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni5Cr (1071/1187 MPa, 50.5%, 59.94 GPa-%). No figure panels, scale bars or error margins are present.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table with 35 data rows and columns YS (MPa), TS (MPa), TEL (%), TS × TEL (GPa-%) and Reference; bottom four rows are the paper's own Fe–20Mn–9Al–1.5C steels labelled 'This study'. All values are legible.

observations.observation: The table reports five quantities per alloy: YS (MPa), TS (MPa), TEL (%), their product TS × TEL (GPa-%), plus a literature Reference number.

The four steels of this study are listed as Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-3Cr (YS 969 MPa, TS 1141 MPa, TEL 54.4%, TS × TEL 62.07 GPa-%), Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni (1202 MPa, 1283 MPa, 34.1%, 43.75 GPa-%), Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni3Cr (1110 MPa, 1206 MPa, 45.9%, 55.36 GPa-%) and Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni5Cr (1071 MPa, 1187 MPa, 50.5%, 59.94 GPa-%).
Within the study's Ni-bearing steels the table shows YS falling from 1202 MPa (2Ni) to 1071 MPa (2Ni5Cr) and TS from 1283 MPa to 1187 MPa as Cr is added, while TEL rises from 34.1% to 50.5%.
Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni has the highest yield strength (1202 MPa) and highest tensile strength (1283 MPa) of every entry in the table.

The largest TS × TEL values in the table belong to reference alloys Fe-30Mn-8Al-1.2C (TRIPLEX steel, 66.45 GPa-%) and Fe-22Mn-0.5C (66.38 GPa-%), both above the best value of the present steels (62.07 GPa-% for Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-3Cr).
The five rows of Fe-28Mn-12Al-1C (TRIPLEX steel, ref [36]) span YS 700-1065 MPa, TS 881-1068 MPa, TEL 28-66% and TS × TEL 29.90-58.14 GPa-%.
Fe-8Al has the lowest strength in the table (YS 210 MPa, TS 281 MPa) with 35% TEL and 9.83 GPa-%.
The caption states that Table 2 gives tensile results for UFCed 3Cr, 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr, 2Ni5Cr steel and reference steels.

The citing text states the total elongation increases from 34.1% to 54.5% on adding Cr to the 2Ni, 2Ni3Cr and 2Ni5Cr steels, whereas the table cell for Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.5C-2Ni5Cr reads 50.5% — the two readings disagree.

The citing text states that the yield strength of the 2Ni steel is 1202 MPa and the tensile strength 1283 MPa, and that the 3Cr steel without Ni reaches 969 MPa and 1141 MPa, matching the table values.
Table values are internally consistent as products: e.g. 1.141 GPa × 54.4% = 62.07 GPa-% for 3Cr and 1.187 GPa × 50.5% = 59.94 GPa-% for 2Ni5Cr.

The citing text argues the strength–ductility combination of the Fe–20Mn–9Al–1.5C-xNi-yCr steels distinguishes them from other steels, especially by a large yield-strength increase at the same GPa-% or total elongation.
Reference alloys are grouped as Fe–Al binary [42], Fe–Mn binary and Fe–Mn–C TWIP [43-47], Al-containing lightweight steels [14,36,48] and stainless steels [49,50].
